description: A high-resolution spatiotemporal wildfire propagation dataset for the Mediterranean and Europe is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Simon Müller et al. Wildfires are becoming more frequent and severe under the influence of climate change, posing increasing risks to ecosystems, human health, and infrastructure. Accurate spatiotemporal data on wildfire propagation is used to advance fire behavior modeling, improve management strategies, and mitigate future impacts. However, existing datasets with both high spatial and temporal resolution are rare, costly, and time-consuming to produce. Coverage: continental; published in 2026. Formats: Shapefile, Image, PDF. The data are held in Zenodo and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support communication-network and digital-infrastructure studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
